project.name: lmr
project.summary: Local Model Router: a Go 1.25 OpenAI-compatible API router in front of Ollama. chi for HTTP, zerolog for logs, SQLite keystore (CGO) for API keys encrypted with AUTH_ENCRYPTION_KEY, and an admin UI of server-rendered HTML in internal/admin/templates/ (Alpine.js + htmx, shared theme.css). Users are developers calling the OpenAI-compatible API (curl, VS Code, SDKs) and operators running it with Docker Compose.
conventions: gofmt (tabs); some existing files are not gofmt-clean, so never reformat unrelated lines
zerolog for logs; openai.WriteError for API errors (OpenAI error shapes)
smallest diff that meets the acceptance criteria; no new dependencies
config keys in internal/config (struct, mapstructure tag, defaults in loader.go) and documented in config.example.yaml

tests.docker: docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/src -w /src golang:1.25 sh -c 'go vet ./... && go test -race ./...'
tests.screenshots: headless Chrome at desktop (1280px) and mobile (390px) widths for any UI change

reviewers.label: sec
reviewers.focus: Security. Check authn/authz on new routes (API key middleware, admin session), secrets in logs or responses, input validation at the HTTP boundary, injection (SQL, template, header, HTML: html.EscapeString / html/template), constant-time comparison of secrets, resource exhaustion (unbounded maps, bodies, goroutines), error messages that leak internals. CHANGES only for high or medium findings; list low ones as notes.

reviewers.label: ux
reviewers.focus: User experience for API users and operators. Does it solve the user's real problem; are errors actionable and in OpenAI error shape; OpenAI compatibility of responses; sensible config defaults and names; README and config.example.yaml updated when behaviour or setup changes; admin flows need no guesswork. CHANGES only when a user would be confused or blocked.

reviewers.label: ui
reviewers.focus: Visual design of the admin UI in internal/admin/templates/ and the HTML fragments rendered in internal/admin/handler.go. Consistency with theme.css tokens and classes (no one-off inline styles), layout at narrow widths, loading/empty/error states, contrast, visible focus, labels on inputs and buttons. If the diff has no UI changes, write VERDICT: PASS and 'No UI changes in this job.'

reviewers.label: code
reviewers.focus: Correctness and code quality. Each acceptance criterion is met and a test proves it; bugs (nil derefs, unchecked errors, races on shared maps or goroutines, leaks); read every caller of a changed function; fits the conventions in project.conventions; no speculative abstractions. Run the tests yourself and add the line `Tests: <command> -> <result>`. CHANGES for any bug or unmet criterion.

escalate_on: a change to the auth middleware or its allow-list, including any new unauthenticated route
a new external resource load (script, font, CDN)
a breaking API or config change
